items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The API types have clear names (ConsistentHashHeader, ConsistentHashCookie, ...) and each field has a doc comment, including the dedup and ordering rules. The logic sits in its own consistent_hash.go file in the plugin pattern. gofmt and golangci-lint fmt were run.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Follows the plugin pattern: types file, an IR built in constructor.go, an apply step in traffic_policy_plugin.go and a merge in merge.go (+48 lines). Codegen came from make go-generate-apis. Keeping a separate list per type means build and merge share the same dedup and ordering.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Inputs are checked at the boundary with CEL and Min/MaxLength/MaxItems markers. An invalid ttl or regex marks the policy as errored rather than being ignored. The agent caught the CEL cost-limit problem and fixed it with MaxLength=32.

items.name: Multi-policy merge semantics
items.evidence: merge.go unions the lists with higher-priority entries first and dedups them. Separate per-type lists keep canonical order. sourceIp is taken from the higher-priority policy even when unset, and merge origins are recorded as "consistentHash". The golden test covers all of this and the hidden tests pass.

items.name: Empty spec and disable handling
items.name_zh: 空配置与 disable 处理
items.evidence: {} produces one sourceIp entry with terminal=false. disable produces nothing and suppresses inherited policies. The CEL rule "!has(self.disable) || !self.disable || (...)" appears in the generated CRD. Edge case: the default is applied after merging, so a {} merged with a policy that has headers gives no sourceIp.
